speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Microphone for questions, please. Thank you. Can  I ask about Patrick Dorgu and his performance? He  
seemed to have end products as well, but also he  was seen asking, telling the referee they didn’t  
think it was a penalty when he won. As a manager,  do you like to see that sportsmanship? It depends.  
It’s the right thing to do. So I’m quite proud of  him, but it depends. I cannot say if he’s nil-nil  
or losing, if I have the same response. So he did  well. He did a great performance. He was improving  
during the game. So he’s learning a lot in that  position. He has the physicality. He’s clearly  
able to play in our league. So it was a good game  and a good action from Dorgu. Ruben, we speak a  
lot about Bruno Fernandes and people criticising  – you said before. Well, today, when you’re losing  
and you need someone to step up, he’s done it  again. Could you just explain what it influenced?  
I think it’s not just the team, it’s the club. We  already spoke about Bruno a lot of times. We know  
that sometimes he’s frustrated. We know that he  wants to win so bad that sometimes when the things  
are not, we are not playing well, he’s changing  position and go after the ball, and sometimes he  
needs to trust a little bit more in his teammates  to allow him to do their job and help him also to  
play better. But when we need it, his will is  there in set pieces. He can change position,  
he can bring the ball forward, he can score goals,  he can make transitions like he showed today  
in the last 10 minutes of the game, he can defend.  So it’s a perfect captain for our team and we need  
to help him to win titles because he deserves  a lot. I felt like Joshua Zirkzee had maybe  
his best game in the year, and if you agreed,  but in that number 10 role, that maybe seems to  
unleash a little bit of what you’re doing since  you’re carrying the ball, in out of possession,  
you need to question for a time. I think all the  team played really well. I think the moments that  
we lost some of the control of the game was  our fault. But I think we did a very complete  
exhibition. We defended quite well, sometimes  one against one at the back. We try to play,  
we show some moments and Josh was part of that. I  think he’s improving – he’s more aggressive when  
he doesn’t have the ball. So if he’s improving  without the ball, that can help Josh a lot with  
the ball because he has the talent. In some  phases, I think he can be more direct. He’s so  
he has a lot of class touching the ball, but  sometimes he needs to think more as a striker.  
I need to score no matter what. It doesn’t  need to be the most beautiful goal or control,  
but he’s improving. Congratulations, Ruben. Was  that the most – was that the best or the most  
complete performance your side has put in since  you came in? And given the injuries, the outside  
noise, everything, how impressed are you by the  resilience? I think I felt during the week that we  
showed that we are ready for these kind of  games. I think our exhibition against Arsenal  
was not beautiful, but helped a lot. That second  half helped us a lot to believe. And then I felt  
that the team, even before the match, was full of  confidence. We suffered a goal, but we continued  
to play the same thing. And that can show that we,  since the first minute, we believed that we could  
go to the next stage. But this is also a different  competition. I think the physicality of our team  
made a great difference in these two games.  Just one second. O.K., Spain. What have been  
the improvements from your team from the tactical  point of view in relation to the games? What have  
been the keys from the tactical point of view?  I think we – we had more time to think. Chelsea  
usually pressed a little bit higher and today we  had more time to think. Again, we suffered a lot,  
especially in our league in some games with the  physicality. We felt that we could let three  
against three in front because we feel that with  our physicality we can recover possession and we  
can deal with the players one against one. So,  everything in this game helped us a lot to play  
better with the ball and without the ball.  Casemiro got a huge ovation when he left the  
pitch. What’s been behind this? I think he’s  improving his game and I’m improving the way  
I should use a player like Casemiro. I’m not  trying to put Casemiro pressing really high.  
I think we are – you can feel that our team  is more connected, even defending. That can  
help a lot, Casemiro, because he’s so smart and  intelligent, reading the game. In short spaces,  
he can understand where the ball is going. So  it’s everything together. The team is better,  
the players can play better. I understand better  the characteristics of the players. So everything  
combined can help us to engage. Evening Ruben,  congratulations. How important was it tonight  
to win this game, not just to win the game, but  what it does for your season? Your season is still  
alive. Yeah, the feeling, and you can feel the  difference, the noise, it’s hard to… to explain.  
You feel the confidence from the supporters, the  players – it was a really good night and we have  
this competition, we have the Premier League –  it gives us a lot of energy and confidence to  
go to our games in the Premier League. And  we feel you can go to the next station and  
we believe that we can go to another stage. This  week was a different week. We dealt with a lot of  
problems of the pressure. We showed the future.  So we finished that. It’s not finished because  
we have a game on Sunday. But this game today was  really good for everybody in the club, the staff,  
the players and especially the fans. And you can  finally enjoy your game. Yeah, it’s – the feeling  
is completely different, not just the result,  but the way we play. So it’s – it’s the same job,  
but it’s completely different. So, but the  good thing and the bad thing is that after  
this game it’s over and tomorrow we are going  to think about Sunday – it’s going to be hard,  
the next game in the Premier League.  Congratulations for the victory. To ask you  
about the three penalties and especially the last  one. And what would you think if this happened on  
the other side? To unite, would you be angry  today? Can you imagine hope? The last one? No,  
I don’t see the image. The last one was Patrick,  that one. Yes, Patrick, if it’s not a penalty.  
What I think is that I never speak about –  and we had the opposite, but when there is no  
penalty, there is no penalty; when it’s a penalty,  should be a penalty. So that’s it. I think VAR  
brings more fairness to the game, but I didn’t  see clearly the image. Okay, thank you. Thank you.
title: Ruben Amorim post-match press conference | Manchester United 4-1 Real Sociedad (Agg 5-2)
